 Learn more Why Equinor stock is back in focus 
 Equinor (OB:EQNR) is in the spotlight after third quarter 2026 results, with higher reported revenue and a swing to US$2.54b in net income, alongside a confirmed third quarter cash dividend. 
 That earnings rebound and higher production guidance are landing in a market that has already rerated Equinor sharply. The NOK447.5 share price is supported by a 12.0% 1 month share price return and an 85.2% year to date share price return, while the 1 year total shareholder return of 94.1% and 5 year total shareholder return of 193.9% suggest investors have been pricing in both income and longer term project execution, as recent deals in lithium and Norwegian offshore partnerships add new angles to the story. 
 Scan how Equinor stacks up against other energy producers on financial strength and price momentum by reviewing the hand picked list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (203 results) 
 After a near doubling in a year and a share price above the average analyst target, the gap between Equinor's rally and fair value estimates has widened. Is the market now ahead of the numbers or still catching up? 
 Most Popular Narrative: 18% Overvalued 
 Equinor trades at NOK447.5 against a narrative fair value of NOK379.9, so the widely followed thesis sees the current rally as running ahead of modeled cash flows while still hinging on long duration oil, gas and power projects. 
 The main thing that has to go right is Equinor successfully executing its NCS 2035 well and tieback program and major international projects while keeping capex overruns, operating cost inflation and rising engineering hours under control. 
 The current valuation implies the market is placing a high value on Equinor's ability to sustain strong cash flow, maintain increased buybacks and deliver on long term growth ambitions without material erosion of returns. 
 See why 99 investors see Equinor as 18% overvalued . 
 Result: Fair Value of NOK379.9 (OVERVALUED) 
 Still, if Equinor delivers on its NCS 2035 program and continues to extract efficiencies from digital tools like DELI and Omnia.Prevent, that could challenge this overvaluation story.
